# CellRank 2: unified fate mapping in multiview single-cell data

## Takeaway

CellRank 2 combines kernel views and graph-based dynamics to estimate terminal states, fate probabilities and lineage-correlated genes. It is useful when the analysis question is a transition or fate question rather than a static cluster comparison.

## Input and output

- Input: .h5ad with neighbors plus a justified transcriptomic, velocity or other kernel view.
- Output: terminal states, fate probabilities, lineage drivers and audit tables.
- Record: kernel choice, root/terminal state assumptions, random seed and data filtering.

## Official material

- DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-024-02303-9
- Code: https://github.com/theislab/cellrank
- Reproducibility: https://github.com/theislab/cellrank2_reproducibility
- Turnkey entry: python/01_cellrank2_template.py.

## Limitation

Fate probabilities are model outputs. They require an explicit dynamical prior and should be stress-tested against alternative kernels and perturbation or time-course evidence.
